observed_text: KV = 25 kT at 300 K (100 s with τ0 = 1e-9 s): Nd2Fe14B (K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³) is a 3.4–3.6 nm sphere, volume 2.1–2.4e-26 m³; magnetite is 24.5 nm on K1 and 56 nm on the cubic barrier K1/12, and is reported at 20–50 nm. Tabulated: Fe 16 nm, Co 7 nm, Ni 34 nm.
implied_text: There is no minimum size. Retention time falls exponentially with the grain's barrier, and a size is quoted for a chosen waiting time.
description: The thermal-stability size of a magnetic grain is a few nanometres for Nd2Fe14B and tens of nanometres for magnetite at room temperature and 100 s.
notes: The first version gave ~30 nm for Nd2Fe14B and said magnetite was smaller; both were wrong. The Nd2Fe14B figure is computed here from sourced K1; no published table for it was opened. value_si is the Nd2Fe14B volume, mid-range.

observed_text: The attempt time τ0 is a fitted constant, usually taken as 1e-9–1e-10 s; values down to 1e-13 s are used. Measurement windows run from 1e-12 s (neutrons) through 1e-9–1e-7 s (Mössbauer) to about 100 s (dc magnetometry).
implied_text: Two clocks, and the effect is their ratio: the attempt time and the observer's window. Blocking is a statement about the observer as much as about the grain.
description: The failure clock is the Néel attempt time compared with the measurement window, not the 28 GHz/T precession carrier.
value_text: τ0 ~ 1e-9–1e-12 s; windows 1e-12 s to years
notes: The same grain can be blocked in one apparatus and unblocked in another.

observed_text: Barrier ΔE = KV for uniaxial anisotropy and K1V/12 for cubic K1 < 0 (magnetite). Nd2Fe14B K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³; magnetite K1 = −1.35e4 J/m³. A 5 nm magnetite particle has an effective anisotropy of 356 kJ/m³, 26 times bulk. An antiferromagnetic matrix raises the blocking of 4 nm Co from 10 K to about 290 K.
implied_text: The barrier is a property of the grain and its surroundings together, not bulk K1 times volume.
description: The barrier that fails is KV, corrected for cubic symmetry, nanoparticle anisotropy and coupling to neighbours.
notes: The first version said the latch hardware is unchanged and only V differs. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: τ = τ0 exp(KV/kT) against the measurement time: ln(τm/τ0) is 25.3 for 100 s, 40.3 for ten years and 2.3 for a Mössbauer window (τ0 = 1e-9 s). Recording media show decay onset at 35 ± 2 and need about 60 for ten-year storage. A 10 % change in diameter changes the retention time about four-thousand-fold.
implied_text: Thermal loss of direction on the observer's clock. Steep in size, with no critical value.
description: Small grains lose their direction on the observer's clock without reaching Tc.
value_text: KV ≈ kT ln(τm/τ0); 25 kT at 100 s
notes: The comparison with a thin-film mirror in the first version is withdrawn. The first version said 25 kT meant hours to years; it means about 100 s. T > Tc is the parent Curie threshold, not this crossover.

observed_text: On the unblocked side coercivity and remanence go to zero and M(H) is reversible, Langevin-like and scales with H/T. 4–5 nm magnetite: 294 Oe and 10.1 emu/g at 5 K against 12 Oe and zero at 300 K. Cooling or measuring faster restores the loop.
implied_text: Stable unblocked output is a zero-remanence ensemble curve plus the blocking surface, not a motor moment.
description: The unblocked grain emits a reversible Langevin curve and a blocking contour, not a usable remanent force.
notes: A single unblocked grain’s fluctuating moment is not a usable motor; the Langevin curve is already an ensemble average. Blocked side is the parent latch.

observed_text: Holding the unblocked state costs no continuous power; the directional memory is simply gone. Zero continuous power on the blocked side as well.
implied_text: Neither the fluctuating unblocked ensemble nor the blocked parent latch draws hold power.
description: Holding either side of the blocking contour costs zero watts.

observed_text: The effective anisotropy of a 5 nm magnetite particle from a Néel–Brown fit is 356 kJ/m³ against the bulk 13.5 kJ/m³. Surface anisotropy, interactions and coupling to neighbours sit between unit-cell anisotropy and the observed blocking temperature.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale Keff step.
description: The volume-and-time collapse does not depend on closing nanoparticle Keff; the mesoscale step remains underived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Brownian relaxation in a fluid is a different machine and is not this entry.

observed_text: A magnet that keeps its remanence in any shape needs a coercivity above half its magnetization: Hc/Ms is 0.75 for the first sintered Nd-Fe-B magnet and below 1e-4 for polycrystalline iron. Single particles of 15–30 nm reverse by thermal activation over one barrier, with an activation volume close to the particle volume. The 25 kBT stability cut is a convention for a 100 s measurement.
implied_text: Minimum hardware is an ordered volume with an anisotropy barrier, down to one single-domain particle. A bulk loop is the sum over a population of grains and walls, each reversing at its own field.
description: The loop needs a latched grain whose barrier outlasts the measurement and whose coercivity exceeds the body's demagnetizing field.
value_text: grain above the thermal cut; Hc above the demagnetizing field; no single loop N
notes: Grain sizes are owned by superparamagnetism. The soft/hard split follows the coercivity and is independent of Tc: iron is ordered up to 1043 K with Hc/Ms below 1e-4.

observed_text: Precession scale γ/2π = 28.025 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). Reversal is thermally activated, so the switching field of a single-domain particle depends on waiting time and temperature. In simulated loops over five decades of sweep rate the coercivity depends on the sweep rate.
implied_text: The latch has a 28 GHz/T precession carrier. The loop itself depends on the clock: a coercivity quoted without a sweep rate and a temperature is a convention.
description: Holding remanence does not run the 28 GHz/T carrier as a power draw; the write field depends on how long and how fast the field is applied.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. The first version named eddy currents as a limit on loop traversal; no opened source supports that and it was dropped.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 is 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³ from fits to magnetization curves; the anisotropy field 2K1/μ0Ms is 6.7–7.7 T. The energy lost per unit volume in one complete cycle is the loop area ∮H dB. A single-bit operation in Permalloy nanomagnets dissipated 1.45 ± 0.35 kBT. Holding a remanent point costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: The barrier that protects remanence is the anisotropy barrier of the permanent-magnet latch. Hold cost is zero. The loop area is the cost of a major-loop write; the measured floor for one bit is of order kBT.
description: Hysteresis is the write/erase cycle of the anisotropy latch: zero hold-power, a major-loop cost equal to the loop area, and a per-bit floor near the Landauer bound.
value_text: K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³; W = ∮H dB per major loop
notes: value_si is the lower edge of the K1 range. K1 = 4.5 MJ/m³ and μ0Ha = 7–8 T of the first version were not found in any opened source. The write field is Hc, about 15–20 % of Ha in sintered Nd-Fe-B; that mesoscale step is the §4.6 gap.

observed_text: Coercivity runs from 0.3–2 A/m (permalloy) through 10–100 A/m (polycrystalline iron) and 136 kA/m (one alnico) to 960 kA/m (first sintered Nd-Fe-B), 5.7 to 6.5 decades. The soft/hard boundary at 1000 A/m, or at about 40 A/m, is a convention.
implied_text: Remanence in an open body is lost when the coercivity is below the body's demagnetizing field. The fall-off along the coercivity scale is continuous, and the metal stays ferromagnetic.
description: The soft limit is a crossover along a six-decade coercivity continuum: loss of a usable write barrier with ferromagnetic order intact.
value_text: Hc from 0.3 A/m to ~10^6 A/m; soft/hard cut at 10^3 A/m by convention
notes: value_si is the conventional class boundary; no measured threshold exists. The first version gave 10^2–10^3 A/m as the typical soft coercivity; typical values are 0.3–100 A/m. Retention in any shape needs Hc > Ms/2.

observed_text: Curie temperature, where the spontaneous magnetization vanishes: iron 770 °C (1043 K) or 1044 K; Nd2Fe14B 585 K in the discovery paper, 585–593 K across three reviews, with 565 K and 558 K in two other opened papers.
implied_text: Thermal destruction of the ordered moment removes the loop. This is a phase transition, distinct from the soft limit and from the volume crossover.
description: No ordered moment above Tc, so no remanent branch and no hysteresis loop.
value_text: T > Tc (585 K Nd2Fe14B, sources 585–593 K; 1043–1044 K Fe)
notes: value_si is the discovery-paper value for Nd2Fe14B. The grain-volume limit is a crossover, filed as superparamagnetism.

observed_text: The first sintered Nd-Fe-B magnet has a remanence of 1.23 T. The energy lost per unit volume in one complete cycle is the area of the loop, W = ∮H dB = ∮H dJ.
implied_text: Stable output is remanence at H = 0 plus a dissipation equal to the loop area each time the major loop is cycled.
description: The loop is the latch cycle: a remanent state at zero field, and dissipation only when the state is cycled.
value_text: Mr at H = 0; W = ∮H dB per major-loop cycle
notes: The loop area is the cost of the major-loop write and is not a floor: a single-domain Permalloy bit has been operated at 1.45 kBT.

observed_text: Holding a remanent point costs zero continuous power: it is a static configuration, and no source reports a dissipation at rest.
implied_text: Zero hold power plus a protocol-dependent write cost is the latch accounting.
description: Holding either remanent branch costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when the state is written.

observed_text: Commercial sintered Nd-Fe-B reaches about 0.2 Ha (1.2 T against 7.5 T, about 15 %); 20–30 % of Ha is the general figure for permanent magnets, and one text puts the overestimate at one order of magnitude. Coherent rotation predicts Hc = 2K1/μ0Ms for an aligned particle. One review reports both a nucleation and a grain-boundary-pinning reading of sintered Nd-Fe-B.
implied_text: QSA has no buffer/barrier specification that produces Hc from nucleation, grain boundaries, local demagnetizing fields and wall pinning. The literature's own form, αHa − Neff·Ms, carries two fitted numbers.
description: Measured Hc is a mesoscale, clock-dependent write field at 15–30 % of Ha. The Curie threshold and the zero-hold-power clause do not depend on closing it.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. The 1.2 T figure is one grade (N50), not a class range.

observed_text: Small grains and ultrathin films lose stable remanence (superparaelectric / depolarization collapse). A single laboratory-stability volume is not claimed; depolarization fields and electrodes enter.
implied_text: Hardware is a polar lattice cell plus a correlated volume large enough that the polar well survives kT and the depolarization field. Ceramic remanence is synchronized output of a poled grain population.
description: One unit-cell dipole is not a macroscopic remanent capacitor; the grain/thickness buffer is real as a class and has no portable number here.
notes: Do not import KV ≳ 25 kT as a ferroelectric constant.

observed_text: The polar displacement is ionic and sits on the lattice-mode clock (optical-phonon / THz class). Macroscopic switching of a ceramic or a multidomain crystal is set by nucleation and wall motion under applied E.
implied_text: The latch carrier is the ionic/phonon clock; ceramic write latency is a slower wall-motion clock.
description: Polar switching does not finish on the phonon period in a real ceramic; the THz class is the local displacement clock.
notes: No numerical phonon frequency is given in the file.

observed_text: A polar double well, locked to a non-centrosymmetric lattice, holds ±Pr at E = 0. Holding remanent P at E = 0 costs zero continuous power. Energy per cycle is ∮E·dP.
implied_text: The latch is the polar well. Energy is spent only on transitions. The write threshold is Ec, not the Landau barrier of a perfect crystal.
description: Remanent polarity is protected by a lattice-locked double well at zero hold-power; write cost is the P–E loop area.
value_text: double well below Tc; write at Ec
notes: Ec of bulk BaTiO3 and PZT-family ceramics is kV cm^{-1} class; the class, not a grade-specific number, is the boundary.

observed_text: BaTiO3 Tc ≈ 120 °C (393 K). Above Tc the room-temperature tetragonal polar phase is gone and remanent P collapses. End-member PbTiO3 Tc ≈ 490 °C.
implied_text: kT closing the polar well destroys the latch. Further BaTiO3 polar-phase changes (~5 °C, −90 °C) are structure changes of an already-latched state.
description: Thermal collapse of the polar latch at the ferroelectric Curie point.
notes: PZT family is composition-dependent; no single PZT Tc is claimed. value_si is the BaTiO3 handbook cliff.

observed_text: Small grains and ultrathin films lose stable remanence. Depolarization field of a uniformly polarized slab is of order P/ε, reduced by electrodes and free charge.
implied_text: Spatial / electrostatic under-provisioning makes P volatile. This is the electrical analog of superparamagnetism, not a portable KV line.
description: Too-small or uncompensated polar volumes erase remanence without reaching Tc.
notes: Dielectric breakdown at larger E is hardware failure of the insulator, not a clean rewrite.

observed_text: Room-temperature spontaneous polarization of single-crystal BaTiO3 along c is Ps ≈ 0.26 C/m². Ceramic remanence is lower; PZT-family Pr remains in the 10^{-1} C/m² class.
implied_text: Stable output is remanent polarization and the associated bound charge / field at E = 0.
description: The polar latch emits a material-typical remanent P, not a linear dielectric that returns to P = 0.
value_text: Ps ≈ 0.26 C m^{-2} (BaTiO3); Pr ~ 10^{-1} C m^{-2} class

observed_text: The sample remains electrically poled at zero continuous field and zero continuous power. Holding remanent P at E = 0 costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Stable remanent polarization and bound charge / field at zero continuous power, inside the Tc / grain / electrode / lattice envelope.
description: Holding remanent polarity costs zero watts. Energy is the P–E loop area only.

observed_text: Ec is microstructure- and thickness-dependent. The superparaelectric size line is not a portable KV/25kT constant: depolarization, screening, and electrodes are extra constraints.
implied_text: QSA does not derive Ec from the Landau well, nor a laboratory-stability volume from node rules.
description: Write threshold and grain/depolarization buffer remain mesoscale data without a closed QSA specification.
value_text: Ec mesoscale; no portable ferroelectric KV
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. kV cm^{-1} class is taken, not derived.

observed_text: Neutron diffraction on MnO at 80 K shows magnetic reflections that are absent at room temperature, from a magnetic cell twice the chemical cell. Two-sublattice accounting: MA ≈ −MB, so Mnet ≈ 0. A single spin is not an antiferromagnet.
implied_text: Hardware is two (or more) interpenetrating sublattices, each a directional latch, correlated over a volume large enough that exchange holds the antiparallel relation against kT.
description: The cancelled latch requires at least two opposed ordered populations, not a single-moment cell.
notes: Readable hardware is the magnetic superlattice (neutron or electron diffraction, resonance), not a dipole field. Size effects are a crossover with no portable length.

observed_text: Antiferromagnetic resonance at low temperature: MnF2 261.4 GHz, MnO 0.82 THz, NiO 1.10 THz, FeF2 1.58 THz. It scales as √(2·HE·HA). kTN/h is 2.5 THz (MnO) and 10.9 THz (NiO).
implied_text: The clock is exchange and anisotropy together: two to three orders above ferromagnetic resonance and well below kTN/h. There is no slow AFM write unless a spin-flop field or an exchange-bias field-cool is imposed.
description: The antiferromagnetic clock is the sub-THz to THz resonance, not kTN/h and not the 28 GHz/T ferromagnetic carrier.
notes: value_si is NiO. The first version said the rate was set by kTN; the measured resonance is 0.10–0.33 of kTN/h.

observed_text: Exchange holds the sublattices antiparallel; anisotropy fixes the axis. The Curie–Weiss temperature θ is 1.1 to 5.3 times TN in the monoxides (MnO 610/116, FeO 570/198, CoO 330/291, NiO ≈2000/525).
implied_text: Two energy scales, not one. A single exchange number does not give both θ and TN. The emergent dipole is ~0 because the sublattices are opposed; cancelled force is the output, not a failure.
description: A latch is a held configuration at zero hold-power, not a requirement of a nonzero dipole.
notes: θ is a Curie–Weiss fit parameter and depends on the fitted window. θ = TN only in the nearest-neighbour two-sublattice mean-field model.

observed_text: Néel temperatures: MnO 118 K (sources 116–120), FeO 198 K (183–200, stoichiometry-dependent), CoO 291 K, NiO 523 K (520–525). Above TN the magnetic reflections are gone and the material is an ordinary paramagnet.
implied_text: Thermal loss of sublattice order → magnetic Bragg intensity gone, Curie–Weiss paramagnet.
description: The cancelled latch dies at TN, the analog of a ferromagnetic Curie point.
notes: A continuous phase transition: sharp in a large crystal, rounded and shifted in thin layers.

observed_text: Spin-flop fields in uniaxial crystals: MnF2 9.3 T, Cr2O3 6.0 T, FeF2 41.9 T; CoO 7.0 T at 240 K. For cubic NiO only 0.24 T (in-plane, computed) and 1.54 T (second-hand) were found; nothing for MnO.
implied_text: A spin-flop field is a field write of the sublattice orientation, not everyday ferromagnetic coercivity. It is a clean threshold only in uniaxial crystals.
description: Fields of 6–42 T rotate the sublattices of uniaxial antiferromagnets; the cubic monoxides show no single clean spin-flop.
notes: value_si is MnF2. The first version claimed tesla-class spin-flop fields for the monoxides without a source.

observed_text: Mnet ≈ 0 on the scale of a ferromagnet of the same sublattice magnetization. The sample exerts no useful permanent-magnet force.
implied_text: Cancelled net moment / ~0 force is the stable output of two opposed latches, not evidence that nothing is latched.
description: The cancelled latch emits approximately zero macroscopic force while the neutron superlattice remains.
notes: Weak canting in some compounds is a small remainder (hematite about 0.4 A m²/kg); it does not convert the family into the permanent-magnet latch.

observed_text: Holding the ordered (cancelled) state costs zero continuous power. There is no hysteresis-heat bill at rest.
implied_text: A static antiparallel superlattice with Mnet ≈ 0, held at zero continuous power below TN.
description: Holding the cancelled latch costs zero watts.

observed_text: The mapping takes the sign of the inter-sublattice coupling as data (the lattice and electronic structure that make J antiferromagnetic).
implied_text: QSA does not here derive why MnO is AFM and Fe is FM. That is a gap in the node rules, not a gap in the latch accounting.
description: The AFM sign of J is taken, not produced from a more primitive node rule.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Weak ferromagnetism/canting is not this gap.

observed_text: The shift is roughly proportional to 1/tFM up to several hundred nm. It is independent of antiferromagnet thickness above about 20 nm and zero at a few nm (6 nm in one IrMn study). The coupling reaches through Ag, Au or Cu spacers up to 50 Å.
implied_text: Hardware is an antiferromagnet thick and anisotropic enough to hold its direction, a ferromagnet thin enough not to dilute the interface term, and proximity within a few nanometres.
description: Two ordered bodies plus a coupling with a reach of nanometres; missing any of the three removes the shift.
value_text: AFM ≳ a few nm; FM thin; separation ≲ 5 nm
notes: The first version said a separated AFM and FM show no shift, with no length.

observed_text: Setting needs a cool through the ordering temperature in a field or from a remanent state; zero-field cooling from a demagnetized state gives no shift. The blocking temperature rises with measurement sweep rate.
implied_text: The pin is set by a thermal write and is itself thermally activated: its blocking temperature depends on the observation clock.
description: Pin-setting latency is a laboratory field-cool; reading the pin depends on the sweep rate.
notes: Training (the shift falls roughly as 1/√n over consecutive loops) is a relaxation of the pin.

observed_text: The loop is centered at −Hex. Co–CoO particles: 1600 Oe at 77 K, up to 9500 Oe at 4–10 K. Interface energy 0.004–0.47 erg/cm² for common pins, up to 3.5 for oxidized Co. A 4 nm Co core that blocks near 6–10 K alone stays blocked to 220–290 K when pinned.
implied_text: The antiferromagnet adds a unidirectional barrier. In a small grain it can be the dominant barrier, not only an offset on an existing latch.
description: Exchange bias is a second, unidirectional barrier that can stabilize the ferromagnet as well as offset its loop.
notes: The ideal-interface (Meiklejohn–Bean) estimate is too large by a factor of 3 to several orders.

observed_text: The shift falls to zero at TB. FeMn 380–480 K (TN 490 K), IrMn 400–520 K (690 K), NiO 450–500 K (520 K), Co/CoO(25 Å) 180 K (291 K). A film has a distribution of blocking temperatures, and TB rises with sweep rate.
implied_text: Thermal unblocking of the pin removes the shift and leaves a centered loop, with coercivity still enhanced up to TN. The ferromagnet stays ordered.
description: The pin unblocks at TB, a rate-dependent crossover that is not the Néel transition.
value_text: T > TB (≤ TN of the layer)
notes: TB ≤ TN holds against the layer's own ordering temperature; annealed polycrystalline FeMn is listed at 420–570 K against a bulk 490 K.

observed_text: The shift falls as 1/tFM. Below a critical antiferromagnet thickness of a few nanometres it drops abruptly to zero; the critical thickness is an order of magnitude smaller for the more anisotropic fluoride.
implied_text: FM-side buffer dilution and AFM-side under-provisioning are the two spatial failures of the nested latch.
description: Too thick an FM film dilutes Hex; too thin an AFM film unblocks the pin.
value_text: H_ex ~ 1/t_FM; AFM too thin → no pin
notes: Ferromagnet dilution is the crossover on this row. The antiferromagnet-thickness limit is a threshold. Damage to the interface is a third failure with no measured scale filed.

observed_text: The hysteresis loop is shifted along the field axis rather than centered at H = 0, generally opposite to the cooling field. In Fe/FeF2 a large cooling field (70 kOe against 2 kOe) reverses the sign.
implied_text: Stable output is an offset −Hex of the FM loop and a remanent FM state whose zero-field point is no longer symmetric.
description: The machine emits a unidirectional loop offset, not a centered remanence.
notes: An increase of FM coercivity often accompanies the shift; the two numbers are not the same artifact.

observed_text: Holding the shifted remanent point costs zero continuous power. Energy is spent to field-cool (set the pin) and to traverse the shifted loop (write the FM).
implied_text: The offset remanent state is a latch: set once, held at zero watts below TB.
description: Holding the shifted remanence costs zero watts.

observed_text: The ideal-interface estimate exceeds the measured coupling by a factor of three to several orders of magnitude; roughness, uncompensated spins, and antiferromagnetic domains are the named ingredients. TB often lies well below bulk TN.
implied_text: QSA does not reduce the interface to a buffer/barrier number, and does not give a portable KV line for TB/TN.
description: Hex and TB/TN remain interface- and grain-level data without a closed specification.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. Loop shifts also occur with pins that are not antiferromagnets.

observed_text: The demagnetizing factors of a uniformly magnetized ellipsoid sum to 1. Sphere: 1/3 on every axis, so ΔN = 0. Infinite wire: 1/2, 1/2, 0. Thin film: 0, 0, 1. For a prolate spheroid ΔN is 0.240, 0.416 and 0.470 at aspect ratios 2, 5 and 10. Reversal is coherent only below a coherence radius of about five exchange lengths (7.4–16 nm in Fe, Co, Ni).
implied_text: The latch cell is a ferromagnetic particle or precipitate with nonzero ΔN, thinner than the coherent diameter and large enough to pass the thermal cut. A sphere has no geometry barrier at any size.
description: Shape latch hardware is an anisotropic body (needle or plate), not a unit cell and not a sphere.
notes: The demagnetizing factors are exact magnetostatics; the spheroid values are computed from Osborn's formula, whose paper was opened as an abstract only. Alnico rods of 40–50 nm exceed the coherent diameter of about 20 nm.

observed_text: Precession scale γ/2π = 28.025 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). Elongated iron particles of 130–305 Å reverse by a non-coherent mode closest to chain-of-spheres fanning; alnico rods of 40–50 nm start to reverse by curling.
implied_text: Geometry changes the barrier and leaves the carrier unchanged. Write latency is set by the field sweep and by the reversal mode.
description: The shape latch uses the same 28 GHz/T precession clock as the crystal-K1 latch.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. The first version listed curling and buckling and omitted fanning.

observed_text: Kshape = (μ0/2)Ms²ΔN. The scale (μ0/2)Ms² is 1.84 MJ/m³ in Fe (2.15 T) and 0.15 MJ/m³ in Ni. The needle maximum for Fe is 0.92 MJ/m³: 18 times iron's own K1 (0.05 MJ/m³), 4.7–5.3 times below Nd2Fe14B (4.3–4.9) and 19 times below SmCo5 (17.2). The maximum shape anisotropy gives a hardness parameter κ = 0.5.
implied_text: The barrier is magnetostatic and geometric. No large K1 is required, and the latch it supplies is semi-hard. Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power.
description: Shape alone latches a high-Ms needle with a barrier of at most 0.92 MJ/m³ in Fe: 18 times iron's crystal K1 and 5 to 19 times below a rare-earth K1.
value_text: K_shape ≤ 0.92 MJ/m³ in Fe (0.44 at 2:1, 0.86 at 10:1); (μ0/2)Ms² = 1.84 MJ/m³
notes: value_si is the Fe needle maximum, half of (μ0/2)Ms². The first version said the Fe scale matched a hard-magnet K1 and that the Ni scale was several times smaller; it is 12 times smaller. Measured switching fields of elongated iron reach 15–19 % of the ideal needle field.

observed_text: ΔN of a prolate spheroid is 0.240 at aspect ratio 2, 0.416 at 5 and 0.470 at 10, against the needle limit 0.5 (48 %, 83 % and 94 % of it). It is zero at aspect ratio 1: a sphere has 1/3 on every axis.
implied_text: The geometry barrier scales with ΔN and goes to zero continuously as the body approaches a sphere, at any volume and any Ms.
description: ΔN falls continuously to zero as the aspect ratio approaches 1; half the needle limit is already reached near aspect ratio 2.
notes: A continuous zero; the first version called it a sharp collapse. Alnico sits on this file with a qualifier (rods thicker than the coherent diameter). Nd2Fe14B does not need shape: its K1 (4.3–4.9 MJ/m³) exceeds its magnetostatic scale (1.03 MJ/m³).

observed_text: The barrier goes as Ms² and vanishes with Ms at the Curie temperature: Fe 1044 K, Ni 628 K. μ0Ms is 2.15 T in Fe and 0.61–0.62 T in Ni, so the Ni scale is 12 times below the Fe scale.
implied_text: The geometry barrier is proportional to Ms². Lose the moment and the needle stops being a latch.
description: Shape anisotropy vanishes with Ms at the Curie point, and is smaller in proportion to Ms² in a weak-moment material.
value_text: μ0 M_s = 2.15 T (Fe); barrier ~ M_s^2; Tc 1044 K (Fe)
notes: The Curie point is the threshold. Between materials the dependence on Ms is continuous. The thermal volume limit is a crossover, filed as superparamagnetism with K = Kshape.

observed_text: Elongated iron particles (150 Å, 3:1) have an intrinsic coercive force of 1600 Oe, and coercive force correlates with elongation; bulk polycrystalline iron has 10–100 A/m. A film magnetizes perpendicular to its plane only when K > μ0Ms²/2; CoFeB/MgO is perpendicular up to a CoFeB thickness of 1.5 nm.
implied_text: Stable output is a uniaxial remanent direction locked to the long axis of a particle, or to the plane of a film, without a large magnetocrystalline K1.
description: The geometry barrier emits long-axis (or in-plane) remanence at zero hold-power.
value_text: M locked to long axis / film plane
notes: 1600 Oe is 127 kA/m. In CoFeB/MgO the reorientation is a threshold at a system-specific thickness of about 1.2–1.5 nm.

observed_text: Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power: it is a static configuration, and no source reports a dissipation at rest.
implied_text: Stable long-axis remanence at zero continuous power, without a large K1.
description: Holding the shape latch costs zero watts.

observed_text: The coercive force predicted for shape anisotropy frequently far exceeds the observed value. Elongated iron reaches 1600–2000 Oe, 15–19 % of the 10.7 kOe of an ideal needle, and reverses by fanning. Alnico rods exceed the coherent diameter, start to reverse by curling and do not reach the Stoner–Wohlfarth limit.
implied_text: ΔN does not predict the measured switching field; this is the same mesoscale Hc gap as on the hysteresis file. The continuous zero of ΔN at aspect ratio 1 does not depend on closing it.
description: Switching-field numbers remain mesoscale: measured values are 15–19 % of the ideal-ellipsoid field.
value_text: H_c ≈ 0.15–0.19 of the ideal needle field (Fe)
notes: File-level mapping was lowered from High to Medium for this reason. This entry owns the ΔN term only; shape and crystal anisotropy add when both are present.

observed_text: Wall width measured in Nd2Fe14B: no wider than 7 and 9 nm (90° and 180° walls) by electron holography, about 6 nm by neutron scattering, 4–9 nm by other methods. By the Bloch formula π√(A/K1) the tabulated widths are 40 nm (Fe), 14 nm (Co), 82 nm (Ni), 3.9 nm (Nd2Fe14B) and 3.6 nm (SmCo5). No direct measurement was found for bulk Fe, Co or Ni.
implied_text: The wall is a finite-width spatial buffer in which the moment rotates between adjacent latched directions.
description: A domain wall is a transition strip of finite width: 4–9 nm measured in Nd2Fe14B, 3.6–82 nm by formula across the tabulated materials.
notes: value_si is the Nd2Fe14B neutron-scattering value. The formula widths are Model: exchange stiffness is inferred and two tabulations differ by 2.4×, which moves a width by 1.55×. The first version's sentence that two domains merge below the wall width had no source and was removed.

observed_text: Precession scale γ/2π = 28.025 GHz/T (CODATA 2022). Near the coercive field wall motion is the dominant magnetization mechanism, and Barkhausen jumps are irregular fluctuations in the motion of a wall.
implied_text: A static pattern has no ongoing clock cost. Pattern changes are wall-motion events that proceed in unpinning jumps set by the defect structure.
description: Domain walls inherit the 28 GHz/T spin carrier; the partition itself changes in pinning-limited jumps.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency. No wall velocity is filed. Damping and eddy currents, named in the first version as limits on wall speed, had no opened source and were dropped.

observed_text: Wall energy by the Bloch formula 4√(A·K1): 2.6 mJ/m² (Fe), 9.3 (Co), 0.5 (Ni), 5.7 (BaFe12O19), 25 (Nd2Fe14B), 77 (SmCo5). A second tabulation gives 1.2 (Fe), 9 (BaFe12O19), 27 (Nd2Fe14B) and 120 (SmCo5). Holding a static domain pattern costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Each domain is the parent anisotropy latch. The wall is a distributed transition whose energy per area is the price of a partition. Pinning of walls at defects is the barrier that appears as Hc in soft material.
description: Partition cost is wall area times 4√(A·K1), 0.5–77 mJ/m² in the tabulation; static patterns have no hold-power bill.
value_text: γ_w = 0.5–77 mJ/m² (Nd2Fe14B 25); zero hold-power at rest
notes: value_si is Nd2Fe14B. The two tabulations differ by 2.2× for Fe, 1.6× for BaFe12O19 and SmCo5, and 1.1× for Nd2Fe14B.

observed_text: Single-domain diameter by 72√(A·K1)/(μ0·Ms²): 12 nm (Fe), 68 nm (Co), 32 nm (Ni), 580 nm (BaFe12O19), 214 nm (Nd2Fe14B), 1528 nm (SmCo5). Micromagnetic calculations give 25 nm for iron cubes. Measured for Nd2Fe14B: about 0.2–0.4 µm. Kittel's first estimates were movable by a factor of ten.
implied_text: Below the single-domain size the pattern does not form and the particle is one latch cell. The size is an energy comparison with a shape-dependent prefactor.
description: The domain pattern gives way to a single domain at a material-dependent size: a crossover running from 12–25 nm in iron to 0.2–1.5 µm in hard magnets.
notes: value_si is the Fe diameter. The prefactor is 72 for a diameter and 36 for a radius. For Fe and Ni the tabulated room-temperature blocking diameter (16 and 34 nm) lies above the tabulated single-domain diameter (12 and 31 nm); the 25 nm micromagnetic value for iron would leave a window of 16–25 nm.

observed_text: Magnetization proceeds by wall motion and by rotation inside the domains. In iron and Fe–Si walls unpin at the coercive field (10–100 A/m in polycrystalline iron) and substantial rotation needs 10^3–10^4 A/m. No opened source gives a saturation field or reports saturation as a sharp transition.
implied_text: An applied field expels the walls and the partition is gone; the local latch remains. The field that removes the last wall is microstructure-dependent.
description: Saturation removes the domain pattern and leaves the local directional latch; it is a crossover with no single field.
value_text: walls displaced at Hc; rotation at 10^3–10^4 A/m (Fe, Fe–Si)
notes: T > Tc removes local order and therefore domains (a threshold). Grain-scale relaxation is superparamagnetism.

observed_text: Walls are imaged by Bitter powder patterns, electron microscopy, Kerr microscopy and magnetic force microscopy. In zero applied field the net moment can be far below saturation even though each domain is locally ordered; at saturation the body is one domain.
implied_text: Stable output is a static partition of the aligned population, with walls of finite width and a net moment set by how closed the pattern is.
description: Domains emit a held partition, not a requirement of a large net dipole.
notes: The measured wall width in Nd2Fe14B is 4–9 nm.

observed_text: Holding a static domain pattern costs zero continuous power: it is a static configuration, and no source reports a dissipation at rest.
implied_text: Hold-power of a static partition is zero. Wall motion around a hysteresis loop dissipates the loop area.
description: Holding a domain pattern costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when walls move.

observed_text: Why one sample shows closure domains, another stripes, another a maze is a magnetostatic-plus-pinning problem. A and K1 are taken as inputs to the wall width and energy; A is inferred, and two tabulations differ by 2.4×. In soft material the coercive field is the field at which walls unpin from defects.
implied_text: QSA does not produce A and K1 from a more primitive buffer, and does not select the imaged pattern from node rules. The mesoscale Hc gap reappears as pinning.
description: Pattern choice and the pinning that sets technical Hc remain mesoscale data; the finite wall width and the single-domain crossover do not depend on closing them.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason.

observed_text: Imaged 180° walls in tetragonal BaTiO3 are atomically sharp, of order one to two unit cells (~0.5 nm class). 90° walls are thicker, still nanometre class (typically a few nanometres). Ferroelectric walls as a class sit in the 1–10 nm range.
implied_text: The wall is a measured spatial buffer, not a mathematical point. Narrower than that and the two domains have merged.
description: A resolved polar domain wall is a nanometre-class strip: ~0.5 nm for 180° BaTiO3, a few nm for 90°, 1–10 nm as a class.
value_text: ~0.5 nm (180° BaTiO3) to few nm (90°); 1–10 nm class
notes: value_si is the nanometre-class order. Do not quote magnetic √(A/K) tens-of-nm as this number.

observed_text: A wall whose normal has a jump in P (head-to-head or tail-to-tail) carries bound charge σ_b = (P2−P1)·n. Neutral 180° walls do not. Charged walls need screening (free charge, defects, or conductivity along the wall).
implied_text: Charged walls are an extra electrostatic buffer the magnetic analog does not carry. Uncompensated bound charge is the same family as slab depolarization.
description: A polar partition must provision screening at charged walls; a neutral 180° wall does not.
notes: Wall conductivity can sit many orders above bulk. Not a nested pin and not a 13th design.

observed_text: A 90° wall also switches the tetragonal c axis and is ferroelastic: strain changes with the wall. 90° walls therefore sit on this partition and on the strain channel of piezoelectricity.
implied_text: 90° walls are the strain face of the polar partition. They support oscillator-grid / piezo as well as polar-latch.
description: A 90° wall emits a strain reconfiguration locked to the partition, not polarity reversal alone.
notes: Supporting on polar-latch and oscillator-grid, same pattern as magnetostriction.

observed_text: The polar displacement is ionic and sits on the lattice-mode clock (optical-phonon / THz class). Pattern changes are nucleation and wall-motion events under applied E (or an optical write channel), far slower than that carrier.
implied_text: A static pattern has no ongoing clock cost. Write latency of a domain pattern is wall motion, not the phonon period.
description: Polar walls inherit the THz ionic clock; the partition itself moves on a much slower pinning-limited clock.
value_text: optical-phonon / THz local; wall motion for the pattern
notes: Optical beam motion of walls is a write channel of this partition, not a photon-energy gate.

observed_text: The wall is a distributed transition whose energy per area is the cost of a partition; 90° walls cost more because they also switch strain. Pinning of walls at grains, electrodes, and charged-wall screening sites is the mesoscale barrier that shows up as Ec on the loop. Holding a static partition costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Each domain is the parent polar well. Partition cost is wall area times wall energy per area. Pinning is the mesoscale Ec gap.
description: Partition cost is wall energy per area; static patterns have no hold-power bill.
value_text: wall energy per area; 90° dearer than 180°; 0 W at rest
notes: No numerical wall-energy density is claimed. Ec remains mesoscale on remanence.

observed_text: Single-domain / no-pattern size: the particle size at which inserting a wall costs more than the electrostatic (depolarization) energy it would save. Reported BaTiO3 classes run from ~10 nm (order / superparaelectric collapse, owned by remanence) to tens of nanometres (single-domain still ferroelectric).
implied_text: Below the wall-vs-depolarization cliff the pattern never forms; the particle is one latch cell, not a partition.
description: The domain pattern dies at a process-dependent no-pattern size; there is no universal millimetre-scale domain period.
value_text: ~10 nm to tens of nm (BaTiO3 class)
notes: Prefactors depend on electrodes, screening, and shape. Not NdFeB ~30 nm. Does not close polar-depolarization-buffer.

observed_text: A large enough applied E drives walls out. The technical poling field is microstructure-dependent and is not the Landau well of a perfect crystal. After the walls are gone the body can still hold remanent P at E = 0.
implied_text: Applied E expels walls → the partition is gone. The local well is still present; remanent P after that step is the parent latch.
description: Poling is destruction of the domain pattern, not of the local polar well.
value_text: E large enough to expel walls (≠ Landau well)
notes: T > Tc removes the polar phase and therefore domains; grain-scale superparaelectric collapse is remanence, below the domain problem.

observed_text: At zero applied field the net polarization can be far below the spontaneous value even though each domain is locally latched. Net P ranges from ≈ 0 (closed pattern) to Ps (walls expelled).
implied_text: Stable output is a static partition of the polar population, with measured nm-class wall width and a net P set by how closed the pattern is.
description: Domains emit a held partition, not a requirement of a large net dipole.
notes: Wall positions are imaged (polarized light, etching, PFM, SHG) and are static at rest.

observed_text: A static domain pattern at rest produces no continuous hysteresis heat. Wall positions are imaged and are static at rest: no continuous power is required to hold a given partition.
implied_text: Hold-power of a static partition is zero. Wall motion around a P–E loop dissipates the loop area owned by remanence.
description: Holding a polar domain pattern costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when walls move.

observed_text: Why one sample shows 90° stripes, another 180° lamellae, another a maze is an electrostatic-plus-elastic-plus-pinning problem. Continuum g and Landau α are taken as inputs to ξ. Wall pinning sets technical Ec.
implied_text: QSA does not produce g and α from a more primitive buffer, and does not select the imaged pattern from node rules. The same mesoscale Ec gap reappears as pinning. Charged-wall screening is an extra constraint.
description: Pattern choice and the pinning that sets technical Ec remain mesoscale data; the wall-width and no-pattern cliffs do not depend on closing them.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason. Does not close polar-depolarization-buffer.
